key_insight: The paper replaces sample-wise rewards with distribution-wise rewards to reduce reward hacking and mode collapse in visual generative model reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical training strategy for improving image fidelity and diversity in diffusion-like generators while keeping outputs aligned with real data distributions.
method: Optimize generative models using distribution-wise rather than per-sample rewards.
Use a subset-replace strategy to update only a small subset of a generated reference set for efficient reward estimation.
Apply RL to post-hoc merge coefficients to reduce train-inference inconsistency from SDE-based RL setups.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports FID-50K improvements across base models, including SiT from 8.30 to 5.77 and EDM2 from 3.74 to 3.52, with qualitative gains in perceptual quality and diversity.
watch_item: The subset-replace and distribution-level reward estimation may add implementation complexity and could be sensitive to how the reference set and update subset are chosen.
paper_title: Optimizing Visual Generative Models via Distribution-wise Rewards
